title: Cartan--Leray descent for a procyclic tower of finite etale torsors
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, put $A=\mathbf F_\ell$, and let $V$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. For every $r\ge0$ let $p_r:V_r\to V$ be a finite etale torsor under the constant cyclic group $G_r=\mathbf Z/\ell^r\mathbf Z$: this means $p_r$ is finite, etale and surjective and the action map $V_r\times G_r\to V_r\times_VV_r$, $(v,g)\mapsto(v,g v)$, is an isomorphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-pc-fibre-product]. Suppose $V_0=V$ and given $G_{r+1}\to G_r$-equivariant transition maps $V_{r+1}\to V_r$ over $V$, compatible with reduction modulo $\ell^r$. Set $G=\varprojlim_rG_r=\mathbf Z_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] and $M^q=\varinjlim_rH^q(V_r,A)$, with pullback transition maps and the induced discrete continuous $G$-action. Cohomology on schemes is ordinary small-etale cohomology of the constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and group cohomology is [def-exc-continuous-cohomology]. There is a natural first-quadrant spectral sequence
$$E_2^{a,b}=H^a_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,M^b)\Longrightarrow H^{a+b}(V,A).$$
If the constant-section maps identify every $H^0(V_r,A)$ with $A$ and $M^q=0$ for $q>0$, the edge maps are isomorphisms $H^a_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,A)\simeq H^a(V,A)$. In degree zero the edge is the constant-section map. In degree one the character $G\to G_1=A$, $g\mapsto g\bmod\ell$, maps to the class of the $A$-torsor $V_1\to V$ under the given action.

proof.text: Work in a sufficiently large fixed universe and a small skeleton of $V_{\mathrm{Et}}$, including the countably many objects and fibre powers used below. The single map $V_r\to V$ is a cover because it is etale and surjective. Choose a nonnegative injective resolution $A_V\to I^\bullet$ in abelian sheaves on this site. For an etale $W\to V$, the slice site is $W_{\mathrm{Et}}$: an etale $V$-scheme over $W$ is an etale $W$-scheme and conversely. Restriction to this slice preserves injectives and the constant sheaf restricts to $A_W$. Thus the section complex $I^\bullet(W)$ computes precisely the ordinary cohomology $H^b(W,A)$, naturally in maps $W'\to W$. A nonnegative injective resolution is also K-injective, so this agrees with the cohomology convention in the statement.

source.place: Tag 03F3, lemma-cohomology-of-open; injective existence: injectives.tex Tag 01DP, theorem-sheaves-injectives

proof.text: Let $W_r^a=V_r^{\times_V(a+1)}$. Form the Cech-resolution double complex $D_r^{a,b}=I^b(W_r^a)$, with horizontal differential the alternating sum of pullbacks along deletion of a factor and vertical differential that of $I$. It is first-quadrant; its commuting differentials give total differential $d_h+(-1)^a d_v$. A transition $t_{sr}:V_s\to V_r$ induces $(t_{sr}^{\times(a+1)})^*:D_r^{a,b}\to D_s^{a,b}$. These maps commute with deletion and with $d_v$, and compose because the $t_{sr}$ do. Each augmentation $I^\bullet(V)\to D_r^{0,\bullet}$ is pullback along $p_r$, and the augmentations commute with every transition since $p_rt_{sr}=p_s$.

source.place: Tag 03AS, lemma-cech-map-into, proof: augmented Cech-resolution double complex

proof.text:
For $g\in G_r$ write $a_g(v)=gv$. Use the left action $g\cdot x=a_g^*x$ on sections and cohomology; this is a left action since $G_r$ is abelian. The torsor isomorphism iterated gives
$$V_r\times G_r^a\simeq W_r^a,\quad(v,g_1,\ldots,g_a)\mapsto(v,g_1v,(g_1g_2)v,\ldots,(g_1\cdots g_a)v).$$
The inverse takes successive displacements of the vertices, unique by the torsor property. Sheaf gluing on this finite disjoint union identifies $D_r^{a,b}$ with $\operatorname{Map}(G_r^a,I^b(V_r))$. Deleting vertex zero sends the first coordinate to $g_1v$ and removes $g_1$; deleting an internal vertex multiplies its two adjacent displacements; deleting the last removes $g_{a+1}$. Consequently the horizontal differential in these coordinates is
$$(d_hc)(g_1,\ldots,g_{a+1})=g_1c(g_2,\ldots,g_{a+1})+\sum_{i=1}^{a}(-1)^ic(g_1,\ldots,g_ig_{i+1},\ldots,g_{a+1})+(-1)^{a+1}c(g_1,\ldots,g_a).$$
Equivariance of $t_{sr}$ sends this chart to the chart with all $g_i$ reduced to $G_r$, and sends coefficients by $t_{sr}^*$. This fixes the action and sign convention throughout.

source.place: Tag 03AZ, lemma-cech-spectral-sequence, torsor-nerve coordinates; explicit agent calculation

proof.text: Take the degreewise colimit $D^{a,b}=\varinjlim_rD_r^{a,b}$. Exactness of filtered colimits implies that taking row or column cohomology commutes with this colimit: apply exactness to kernels, images, and the quotient of cycles by boundaries. For each fixed $b$, injective Cech acyclicity says that the augmented row $I^b(V)\to D_r^{\bullet,b}$ has $H^0=I^b(V)$ and $H^a=0$ for $a>0$. Its transition maps on $H^0$ are identity by the commuting augmentations in Step 2. The same assertions therefore hold for $D^{\bullet,b}$. The second spectral sequence of $D$ has only the Cech-degree-zero row-cohomology terms, namely the complex $I^\bullet(V)$. Its finite filtration consequently identifies $H^n(\operatorname{Tot}D)$ with $H^n(I^\bullet(V))=H^n(V,A)$; the identification is induced by the augmentation, since its map on this sole surviving graded piece is identity. There are only $n+1$ summands in total degree $n$, so no unbounded-totalization or inverse-limit assertion is involved.

source.place: Tag 03AW, lemma-injective-trivial-cech; algebra.tex Tag 00DB, lemma-directed-colimit-exact; homology.tex Tag 0132, lemma-first-quadrant-ss

proof.text:
Column cohomology of the Cech-resolution complex is Cech cochains of the presheaf $W\mapsto H^b(W,A)$. In the finite disjoint-union coordinates of Step 3 this gives $H_v^b(D_r^{a,\bullet})=\operatorname{Map}(G_r^a,H^b(V_r,A))$: finite products commute with kernels and images component by component. Applying filtered-colimit exactness once more gives
$$H_v^b(D^{a,\bullet})=\varinjlim_r\operatorname{Map}(G_r^a,H^b(V_r,A)).$$
The induced differential is the formula of Step 3 on cohomology, and the transition sends $c$ to $t_{sr}^*c$ after reduction of every argument. Each class represented at level $r$ is fixed by $\ker(G\to G_r)$; hence $M^b$ has the required discrete continuous action. This uses no injectivity of cohomological pullback.

source.place: Tag 03AZ, lemma-cech-spectral-sequence, column computation; algebra.tex Tag 00DB, lemma-directed-colimit-exact

proof.text: Apply the finite-quotient cochain-colimit comparison with $U_r=\ell^r\mathbf Z_\ell$, $Q_r=G_r$, and $N_r=H^b(V_r,A)$. These $U_r$ are a cofinal descending open-normal basis; the equivariance required of coefficient transitions is exactly that checked in Step 3. It identifies the whole horizontal complex $H_v^b(D)$, including its differential, with $C^\bullet_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,M^b)$. The continuous-cochain/derived-invariants comparison therefore identifies $H_h^aH_v^b(D)$ with $H^a_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,M^b)$. The first spectral sequence of $D$ now has the asserted $E_2$ page and abuts, by Step 4, to $H^{a+b}(V,A)$. First-quadrant convergence supplies a finite filtration in every total degree.

source.place: Tag 0DVG, section-continuous-group-cohomology; homology.tex Tag 0132, lemma-first-quadrant-ss; agent tower application

proof.text: The construction is natural for compatible equivariant maps of the torsor towers: pullback on each nerve commutes with all face maps and with the common augmentation. The displayed finite-quotient comparison is natural as well. To change the injective resolution, use the homotopy equivalence of K-injective resolutions under $A_V$; applying evaluation on every nerve gives a comparison of double complexes. It induces the canonical identity on every $H^b(W,A)$, hence the same comparison on $E_1$ and on all later pages. Homotopic comparison maps give identical column-cohomology maps. Functoriality of the double-complex spectral sequences and the augmentation then gives the identity on $H^n(V,A)$. Thus the spectral sequence from $E_2$ onward and its edge maps are independent of this choice and natural for the tower data.

source.place: Tag 0132, lemma-first-quadrant-ss and functorial filtered-complex construction; resolution comparison: injectives.tex Tag 079P

proof.text: Under the additional hypotheses, all $M^b$ with $b>0$ vanish, and $M^0=A$ via the given constant-section maps. Deck transformations fix constants, so the $G$-action on $M^0$ is trivial. The first spectral sequence is concentrated on its bottom row at $E_2$, and the first-quadrant row-collapse lemma gives the edge isomorphisms $H^a_{\mathrm{cont}}(G,A)\simeq H^a(V,A)$. In degree zero the augmentation used throughout is pullback of sections; the class of $a\in A$ is represented on every $V_r$ by the same constant section. Descent identifies it with the constant section $a$ on $V$, proving the specified degree-zero normalization.

source.place: Tag 0132, lemma-first-quadrant-ss, single-row degeneration; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03AS, augmentation

proof.text: For degree one, the character $\chi(g)=g\bmod\ell$ is represented already at level $r=1$ by the function $G_1\to H^0(V_1,A)$ sending $g$ to the constant $g$. In the chart $(v,g)\mapsto(v,gv)$ of Step 3 its Cech representative on $V_1\times_VV_1$ is the unique displacement $c(v_0,v_1)$ such that $v_1=c(v_0,v_1)v_0$. The identity $c(v_0,v_2)=c(v_0,v_1)+c(v_1,v_2)$ proves it is a cocycle; equivariance makes its pullback to every later nerve the representative of the inflated character. In the resolution double complex it lies in bidegree $(1,0)$ through $A_V\to I^0$, so the bottom-row edge is exactly its Cech-to-cohomology image followed by the inverse augmentation of Step 4. The finite-etale torsor is a torsor for the constant sheaf, and its tautological local section over $V_1$ has these transition sections: the second projection equals $c$ acting on the first. The torsor/$H^1$ comparison identifies their Cech class with the class of $V_1\to V$. Thus the image is this torsor class with the positive displacement convention, also when $\ell$ is odd.
